content: Never mock the gray-headed elder; the greatest wisdom rests within weathered and scarred skin.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: At hárum þul hlæðu aldregi (Hávamál, Stanza 134) — Poetic Edda
explanation: Youth is proud of its smooth skin, quick legs, and sharp teeth, easily dismissing the slow gait and wrinkles of old age. But that elder has survived famines, winters, wars, and heartbreaks that would shatter an unseasoned youth. Sit at their feet and listen.
practicalInsight: Treat an older person with deep, attentive reverence today. Ask for their perspective before making assumptions.
reflectionPrompt: Have you been dismissing the lived experience of elders in your family or field because they move more slowly than you?
